ads_ratio.reason: MICC is a direct multi-listing of ordinary shares, not an ADS program: one NYSE-traded MICC share is one ordinary share (the 612,259,739 issued ordinary shares match the DEI outstanding count in dcf_numbers.json), so per-share figures from the 20-F are directly comparable to the traded price with no scaling.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-18), cover page: securities registered under Section 12(b) are 'Ordinary Shares, nominal value EUR 3.50 per share', trading symbol MICC on the New York Stock Exchange; admission announcement 8 December 2025: issued share capital on admission was 612,259,739 ordinary shares admitted to trading on Euronext Amsterdam, the London Stock Exchange and the NYSE, with DTC accounts credited with interests in TMICC ordinary shares — the NYSE security is the ordinary share itself

moat_against: Category grows only 3-4%/yr and faces a structural GLP-1 appetite headwind; private label and Froneri (valued ~EUR 15B in Oct 2025) contest every shelf

Standalone economics unproven: carve-out ROIC (20.9%/22.3%) was earned on a debt-free allocated capital base; the listed company carries EUR 2,967M net debt (2.4x adjusted EBITDA) and structurally higher standalone costs (interest paid EUR 130M in FY2025)
Unilever retains 19.9% and has committed to sell it within five years (registered for resale April 2026) — a persistent share overhang

Ben & Jerry's governance conflict inherited at the demerger: independent board removed, co-founder resigned Sept 2025, federal litigation live, a founder buy-back campaign valuing the brand at $1.5-2B
Commodity exposure (cocoa, dairy, sugar) and emerging-market FX (incl. Turkiye hyperinflation loss EUR 31M in FY2025) squeeze the ~34.6% gross margin
moat_for: Global scale leader: ~21% share of the global retail ice cream market, #1 position, 30 factories — procurement and cold-chain cost advantage

Power-brand portfolio: Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto and the Heartbrand (Wall's) — proven pricing power (+2.6% price with +1.5% volume in FY2025; gross margin stable ~34-35% through commodity inflation)
Proprietary freezer-cabinet estate and route-to-market in impulse channels — physical distribution moat competitors must rent or replicate
Innovation cadence: 150 launches in 2025 (Magnum Utopia, Cornetto Max, Bonbons bites) driving high-single-digit organic growth in the Magnum and Cornetto brands
moat_justification: World's largest ice cream company (~21% of the global retail ice cream market) with four power brands (Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Heartbrand/Wall's), a proprietary freezer-cabinet estate and cold-chain scale no rival matches globally. Evidence: gross margin held 34.08% / 34.91% / 34.63% across FY2023-25 (fundamentals.json, as filed in EUR) through cocoa/dairy inflation, with +2.6% price growth AND +1.5% volume growth in FY2025 — real pricing power. The roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json reads 20.92% (FY2023) and 22.28% (FY2024), but those are carve-out years: invested capital carried almost no debt and Unilever allocated costs, so they overstate the standalone franchise; FY2025's 214.27% is a demerger artifact (equity fell to EUR 633M when EUR 2,967M of net debt was pushed onto the new balance sheet) and is not evidence. On a standalone capital base the true through-cycle ROIC is unproven — that, plus a category growing only 3-4%/yr, caps the score at 6 (moderate) rather than 7+.
name: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V.
one_liner: World's largest ice cream company (Magnum, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Wall's/Heartbrand), moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $18.78: weighted IRR 9.14% (Tier D; bear-to-bull band D to C), weighted IV@15% $9.84; clears 15% only below ~$9.84, and even the $1.11 pro-forma median base is a carve-out construct — the demerger year (FY2025) printed OE/share of $0.17 after separation costs and new standalone interest, so the honest range runs from deep-D on the latest year to D on the median.
sector: Consumer Staples / Ice cream & frozen desserts

shares_override.reason: Demerger pro-forma denominator. The 20-F states: 'Prior to 6 December 2025, the Group was under the control of Unilever and did not have any issued shares. Accordingly, EPS has not been calculated for prior years.' FY2023-24 are combined carve-out years with no filed diluted share count under any tag (DATA_GAP:shares). The only diluted count the filer has ever filed — 615.6M, the count created at the demerger (612,259,739 ordinary shares issued 6-7 Dec 2025) — is applied to the two missing carve-out years so per-share OE is stated on the capital structure that exists now. Kind is estimate (not filing) because the value is filed for 2025, not for the missing periods; it anchors exactly on the last filed diluted value (615.6M, 1.00x — inside the 0.1x-10x band).
shares_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-18), EPS note (Annual Report p.115): average number of shares 612.3M basic, plus 3.3M dilutive effect of share-based compensation plans = 615.6M diluted average for 2025; the note states the 2025 average equals the shares outstanding at 31 December 2025 and that no EPS was calculated for prior years
